title: NVIDIA's DSX Ready Brings Power and Cooling Into the AI Factory Blueprint
key_facts: NVIDIA's DSX Ready program, announced 21 Sep, sets qualification requirements for battery energy storage systems (BESS) and coolant distribution units (CDUs) used with its DSX AI factory designs.
First qualified BESS suppliers: Hitachi Energy, LG Energy Solution and Tesla; first CDU suppliers: Vertiv, LG Electronics and LiquidStack (2.3 MW to 14 MW).
BESS qualification has 12 tests covering electrical stability, dynamic response, operating transitions and control systems, not just capacity.
The AI buffering test requires tracking workload power ramps within 2% of the commanded ramp.
Trane introduced two 250 MW AI factory cooling reference designs that could free up to 22 MW of electrical capacity for computing.
Qualification applies to individual products and does not replace site engineering, integration or commissioning.
Chris Malone, formerly of OpenAI, Meta and Google, joined NVIDIA as vice president of the DSX Platform.
quote_evidence: Qualification applies to defined products and technical boundaries, while developers remain responsible for site-level design, integration and commissioning.
The company has established twelve tests covering electrical stability, dynamic response, operating transitions and control-system performance.
why_it_matters_hint: Nvidia is extending its influence from chips into the power and cooling kit around them.
